Sarata Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sarata, Ukraine

Not demolished. Little is documented about this cemetery directly, though it appears on Sarata's own Yizkor (memorial) book memory map showing the town's interwar layout; per a 1994 Jewish Preservation Committee expedition, the last burial occurred in 1950, after which the postwar Jewish population used the municipal cemetery instead. Jewish community mentions date to the mid-19th century; about 150 families settled in the early 20th century, mostly renting homes and engaging in commerce and agriculture, owning market stalls. A 1920s Beit Ha-Am served as a holiday synagogue and hosted Zionist activities and Yiddish theater performances; some Jews owned private libraries. Zionist youth movements Beitar and Gordonia remained active until Soviet occupation in 1940. Population reached 316 (12%) by 1930; 1930s German-resident antisemitic propaganda preceded the community's decimation during the Holocaust. A small Jewish population remained in Sarata as of 2005.
